title: No release date per wave in the deck or the split plan
source: 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Executive Presentation CTO v3.pptx; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (legacy only)
description: The deck gives a release date per programme and per story, but no release date and no gate date per delivery wave (0 to 4). The wave slide therefore carries a placeholder.
evidence: split_plan.json legacy entries carry wave, disposition, primary, patterns and slices but no release; the deck names only 28 October 2026, 2 November and November 2026
proposed: When the Wave 4 planning baseline is fixed, take each wave date from the earliest story release inside the wave and record it in the Service Story Catalog and the Day-1 Work Allocation.

title: Version 3 deck describes the monolith; Architecture v5 describes 19 services
source: 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Executive Presentation CTO v3.pptx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
description: Version 3 states one service, one repository, programmatic workflow with no Temporal, one recovery schema and reporting to a data lake. Architecture v5 states 19 services, a shared Temporal layer, one schema per service and no data lake.
evidence: Version 3 slide 2 (DT07, DT08, DT09), slide 3 (recovery schema, 108 entities) and slide 5 (reporting to the data lake) against Architecture v5 slides 13 to 20, 41 and 45
proposed: Keep the version 3 slides word for word, mark the section as version 3 content, and name the decision that changes each statement in the new section (R3 precedence).

title: No accountable team named per service
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R1 U3 and R5.3
description: The Ownership Map fixes the owning service for every table, endpoint, event, workflow and job, but not an accountable team per service. Ownership is soft, by work type, and no person may be named.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 Services sheet has code, service, name, wave, schema, REST base, topic, queue only; R5.3 gives a suggested owner per work type, not per service
proposed: Show the service code of the Ownership Map as the owner and the work-type suggested owner beside it (DL46); revisit only if the programme wants an accountable team per service.

title: Nineteen legacy keys carry no wave value
description: Nineteen entries of the legacy map have no wave value. They are the new platform keys N001 onwards and the new integration keys, which take their wave from the platform or integration epic.
evidence: split_plan.json legacy: 8 entries with wave 0, 19 entries with no wave, the rest 1 to 4
proposed: Take the wave from the service epic or the integration epic (R4, R5.1) and record it in the Service Story Catalog.
